intro: How North American meters are read. C12.19 keeps everything a meter knows in numbered tables. C12.18 reads and writes those tables through the optical port, after a logon and a password. C12.22 carries the same table services over a network.

identify.title: Identify
identify.text: The laptop sends Identification at 9600 baud, 8N1. The meter confirms each packet with one byte, 0x06 (ACK), then answers. Each packet ends with a 2-byte CRC, which this lesson leaves out.

logon.title: Log on
logon.text: Logon names the user, for the meter's log. Security sends the 20-byte password. Only now may the laptop read or write protected tables.

read.title: Read table 23
read.text: A full read of table 23, Current Register Data: 12 bytes and a checksum. What the bytes mean is in other tables: ST 0 says how numbers are coded, ST 21 how many there are, ST 12 and ST 22 what they measure.

end.title: Log off
end.text: Logoff ends the session, Terminate ends the conversation. Without them, the meter keeps the session open until a timeout.

network.title: Over the network
network.text: Later, the head-end reads the same table with C12.22. The same service, 30 00 17, now travels in an ACSE message on port 1153. No logon is needed: each message carries its own security.

frames.c1222-read: Send me all of table 23 (over the network)

notes.ident-ok: The answer starts with 0x00 (OK), then the protocol (0x00: C12.18), its version and its revision. Newer meters also list optional features. Next the laptop could send Negotiate (0x60 to 0x6B) for a higher speed or bigger packets; here it keeps the defaults.
notes.c1222-read: An ACSE message (tag 0x60) on UDP or TCP port 1153. Its header names the meter (called AP title), the head-end (calling AP title) and this request (calling AP invocation ID). Its user information holds EPSEM: a control byte that sets the security mode, then the same service as on the optical port, 30 00 17. In the secure modes, AES-128 in EAX' mode authenticates the message, or authenticates and encrypts it, with a key the meter knows.
notes.c1222-table: An ACSE message back to the head-end. Its header lets the head-end match it to the request. Inside is the same answer as on the optical port: 0x00 (OK), the count, the 12 bytes of table 23 and their checksum.

stp.name: STP
stp.note: 0xEE starts every packet. A 2-byte CRC (CCITT polynomial) ends it; it is not shown here.

ctrl-1.name: Control
ctrl-1.note: 0x20: the toggle bit is 1. Each side flips it with every new packet, so a packet sent twice can be spotted.

seq.name: Sequence number
seq.note: 0: no more packets follow. A message too big for one packet comes in several, counted down to 0.

len-1.name: Length
len-1.note: 0x0001: one byte of data. Numbers in the packet are sent most significant byte first.

ident.name: Identification
ident.note: 0x20: the first service of every session.

logon.name: Logon
logon.note: 0x50: start a session as a named user.

user-id.name: User ID
user-id.note: 0x0002: a number the meter writes into its event log.

password.name: Password
password.note: 20 bytes: "tech2026" and 12 spaces. It crosses the optical port in clear.

ok.name: OK
ok.note: Response code 0x00: OK. 0x01 is an error; 0x03 means this password does not allow it.

table-23.name: Table 23
table-23.note: 0x0017 = 23: ST 23, Current Register Data. Manufacturer tables add 2048: MT 23 is 0x0817.

sum-0.name: Summation 0
sum-0.note: 6 bytes, low byte first, as ST 0 of this meter says. 0x00BC614E = 12 345 678 Wh delivered.

sum-1.name: Summation 1
sum-1.note: 0x01E240 = 123 456 Wh received: energy the house sent to the grid.

cksum.name: Checksum
cksum.note: 0x72: the table bytes and this byte add up to 0, modulo 256.

facts.standard: ANSI C12.18 (optical port), C12.19 (tables), C12.22 (networks); also IEEE 1701, 1377, 1703
facts.transport: Optical port at 9600 baud, 8N1; C12.22 over UDP or TCP 1153
facts.security: C12.18: a 20-byte password in clear. C12.22: AES-128 (EAX') for each message
facts.model: Tables: standard (ST 0, ST 1, ST 23 …) and manufacturer (MT, from 2048)

tips: Read ST 0 first. It says how numbers are coded and in which byte order; without it, table 23 is just bytes.
Many meters count wrong passwords and lock the port for a while. Check the password before you try again.
A table larger than one packet comes in several. Wait for sequence number 0, or read the table in parts with a partial read (0x3F: an offset and a count).
Manufacturer tables (MT, from 2048) are laid out as each maker chooses. You need the maker's documentation to read them.

playground.file: The tables this meter has. A C12.19 reader learns them from ST 0, then reads what it needs by number.
playground.st0: Read it first: how numbers are coded, in which byte order, and which tables exist.
playground.st1: Who made the meter: a 4-letter maker code, the model, hardware and firmware versions, and a serial number.
playground.procedures: Procedures, such as a demand reset or setting the clock, start with a write to ST 7. Their results come back in ST 8.
playground.st12: What each source measures: here, energy delivered and received, in Wh.
playground.st21: How many values the register tables hold. It fixes the size of ST 23.
playground.st22: Which source each summation in ST 23 comes from.
playground.st23: The table this lesson reads: two totals of 6 bytes each.
playground.mt: Manufacturer tables: their number plus 2048. The maker decides what is in them.
